title: PrefillProbe: phase-aware kernel hinting and lightweight autotune
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Goal: build a low-overhead, phase-aware probing and hinting layer (PrefillProbe) that collects a tiny prefill sketch and returns a short-lived kernel hint to the scheduler to improve initial kernel choice for mixed-architecture and mixed-sequence-length workloads.

Rationale: our existing kernel autotuners either (a) require heavy microbenchmarks, (b) warm-start from global profiles that miss tenant-specific patterns, or (c) probe during steady-state which misses prefill decode handoffs. Many latency tail events occur on the first decode tokens when the runtime picks a suboptimal kernel tier. PrefillProbe aims to reduce that first-10-token latency by informing the kernel selector with an ephemeral, per-request hint without compromising throughput or adding long-running profiling overhead.

Scope: implement a lightweight client-side/edge probe that extracts three features within the prefill path (arch fingerprint, effective sequence-length estimate, and input sparsity estimate) in <200 microseconds; a compact hint encoding (2-3 bytes) carried in request metadata; a scheduler hook that prefers hinted kernels for the first N decode steps with a safety rollback policy; telemetry and dashboards showing per-model, per-customer improvement and probe overhead.

Key design goals and constraints:
- Probe overhead budget: <=200 microseconds p99 in prefill path.
- Memory: hint state must be ephemeral and freed after request completion.
- Safety: if hinted kernel violates latency SLO on first decode, immediately fall back to default kernel and record metric.
- Privacy: no persistent customer data leaves request context; hints are anonymized fingerprints.
- Cold-start: warm-start hints via historical tenant traces but allow fast decay to handle drift.

Non-goals: full continuous online autotuner or cross-tenant cache warming. PrefillProbe is advisory and constrained to initial kernel choice handshake between prefill and decode phases.
tasks: Design microspec for prefill sketch features and encoding (Anya)
Implement lightweight probe in prefill codepath (Liam)
Add scheduler hook to accept hint and apply kernel preference for first N decode steps (Anders)
Create rollback safety net that measures first-decode-latency and switches kernels on threshold breach (Sana)
Benchmarks: run microbench suite across A100/V100/RTX architectures with seq-len buckets [8,32,128,512] (perf team)
Telemetry: add probe/decision traces to Console (observability integration)
Canary rollout: feature-flagged, 1% tenants -> 10% -> 50% with bump criteria (SLA checks)
Write runbook for debugging hint mismatches and probe timeouts
acceptance_criteria: Probe adds <=200us p99 wall time to prefill path for 95% of models in microbenchmarks
First-decode tail (p99) improves by >=8% for tested mixed-load scenarios on A100 and RTX when using hints
Hint encoding fits within 3 bytes and passes privacy review
Rollback triggers observed and logged when hinted kernel exceeds latency threshold; observed false-positive rollback rate <2%
End-to-end canary run shows no increase in error rate or token misordering across 48h
notes: Tradeoffs considered: richer probes (per-layer activation stats) were rejected due to overhead and memory pressure on multi-tenant GPU hosts.
We prefer a conservative hint (kernel tier + seqlen bucket ID + architecture hash) rather than absolute kernel IDs to keep compatibility across model variants.
Tie-in with existing warmstart: historical tenant profiles will seed initial hint probabilities but PrefillProbe can override when runtime probe disagrees.
We will reuse existing kernel-metrics counters and add a lightweight histogram for hint->chosen-kernel outcomes.
